name: IE
title: Ireland Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in Irish politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with Fine Gael, Fianna Fáil, Sinn Féin, the Greens, Labour and the Social Democrats, plus your framing bias.
keywords: Irish political quiz, Ireland compass test, Sinn Féin Fine Gael Fianna Fáil, Ireland election 2026, political alignment test Ireland, Irish party quiz

fg.name: Fine Gael
fg.desc: Your answers most closely align with Fine Gael. You favour a pro-business environment, low corporate taxes, fiscal restraint, and socially progressive values.

ff.name: Fianna Fáil
ff.desc: Your answers most closely align with Fianna Fáil. You represent a centrist republican position that balances support for business with state-backed housing initiatives.

sf.name: Sinn Féin
sf.desc: Your answers most closely align with Sinn Féin. You strongly advocate for Irish reunification, massive state builds in housing, wealth taxes, and protecting Irish neutrality.

grn.name: Green Party
grn.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Green Party. You prioritise aggressive carbon reduction, cycling infrastructure, and sustainable economic reform.

lab.name: Labour Party
lab.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Labour Party. You support workers' rights, enhanced public services, and progressive social taxation.

sd.name: Social Democrats
sd.desc: Your answers most closely align with the Social Democrats. You want universal healthcare (Sláintecare), strict political accountability, and massive public housing investment.

ind.name: Independent
ind.desc: Your answers do not strongly align with a single party. You hold pragmatic, local, or mixed views typical of Ireland's large independent voting base.

bank.q: The state should build council and public housing on a massive scale to end the crisis.
bank.ctx: 'Council housing' is government-owned rental housing. This supports building it on a massive scale to end Ireland's housing crisis.

bank.q: The housing fix is backing private developers and cutting red tape, not more state building.
bank.ctx: This argues the fix is backing private developers and cutting red tape, not more state building.

bank.q: A long-term rent freeze should be imposed to protect tenants.
bank.ctx: A 'rent freeze' legally stops rents from rising. This supports a long-term one to protect tenants.

bank.q: Rent freezes drive landlords out and worsen the shortage for everyone.
bank.ctx: This argues rent freezes drive landlords out of the market and worsen the shortage for everyone.

bank.q: Ireland is taking in too many asylum seekers and immigration should be cut.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland is taking in too many asylum seekers and that immigration should be cut.

bank.q: Ireland, a nation of emigrants, has a duty to welcome people fleeing hardship.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland, historically a nation of emigrants, has a duty to welcome people fleeing hardship.

bank.q: Communities should have a real say before asylum centres are placed in their area.
bank.ctx: This argues local communities should have a real say before asylum-seeker centres are opened in their area.

bank.q: Local vetoes over asylum housing just give cover to intimidation and racism.
bank.ctx: This argues letting communities veto asylum housing gives cover to intimidation and racism.

bank.q: There should be a referendum on a united Ireland within the next decade.
bank.ctx: A 'united Ireland' would join the Republic with Northern Ireland (currently part of the UK). This wants a referendum ('border poll') on it within a decade.

bank.q: A border poll now would be divisive and destabilising, and should not be rushed.
bank.ctx: This argues a border poll now would be divisive and destabilising and should not be rushed.

bank.q: Ireland should hold firmly to its military neutrality and stay out of NATO.
bank.ctx: Ireland is militarily neutral and not in NATO (the Western defence alliance). This supports holding firmly to that neutrality.

bank.q: In a dangerous world Ireland can no longer freeload on others’ defence and should deepen western alliances.
bank.ctx: This argues neutrality means freeloading on others' defence, and that Ireland should deepen ties with Western allies.

bank.q: Ireland should move to a single-tier public health system and end private care in public hospitals.
bank.ctx: Ireland has a mix of public and private care. This supports moving to a single-tier public system and ending private care in public hospitals.

bank.q: Private healthcare relieves pressure on the public system, and abolishing it would make waits worse.
bank.ctx: This argues private healthcare relieves pressure on the public system and abolishing it would make waits worse.

bank.q: The wealthiest and highest earners should pay significantly more tax.
bank.ctx: This supports significantly higher taxes on the wealthiest people and highest earners.

bank.q: Higher taxes on the successful just drive investment and talent out of Ireland.
bank.ctx: This argues higher taxes on the successful drive investment and talent out of Ireland.

bank.q: Ireland’s low corporate tax rate is vital and must be protected.
bank.ctx: Ireland's low corporate tax rate attracts multinational companies. This argues it is vital and must be protected.

bank.q: Ireland’s low corporate tax is a race to the bottom that starves public services.
bank.ctx: This argues the low corporate tax is a 'race to the bottom' that starves public services of revenue.

bank.q: Ireland must cut emissions faster, including from its large farming sector.
bank.ctx: This supports cutting emissions faster, including from Ireland's large farming and cattle sector.

bank.q: Climate rules that punish Irish farmers threaten rural life for tiny global gain.
bank.ctx: This argues climate rules that hit Irish farmers threaten rural life for tiny global benefit.

bank.q: Irish farmers are unfairly targeted by climate policy and deserve more protection.
bank.ctx: This argues Irish farmers are unfairly targeted by climate policy and deserve more protection.

bank.q: Farming must meet the same environmental standards as everyone else, not be exempted.
bank.ctx: This argues farming must meet the same environmental standards as everyone else, not be exempted.

bank.q: Legalising abortion in 2018 was the right decision for Ireland.
bank.ctx: In a 2018 referendum Ireland legalised abortion. This defends that as the right decision.

bank.q: Legalising abortion was a moral wrong, and Ireland went too far.
bank.ctx: This argues legalising abortion was a moral wrong and that Ireland went too far.

bank.q: The Irish language should be actively promoted and given more support.
bank.ctx: This supports actively promoting and funding the Irish (Gaelic) language.

bank.q: Compulsory Irish and heavy spending on the language are a waste that few actually use.
bank.ctx: This argues compulsory Irish and heavy spending on the language are wasteful since few people use it.

bank.q: The Catholic Church should have no role in running schools and hospitals.
bank.ctx: The Catholic Church still runs many Irish schools and hospitals. This argues it should have no such role.

bank.q: The Church’s role in Irish education and care is part of the country’s heritage and does good.
bank.ctx: This argues the Church's role in Irish education and care is part of the country's heritage and does good.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with Irish values.
bank.ctx: This argues Islam clashes with Irish values. Supporters cite integration concerns; critics call it religious prejudice.

bank.q: Muslim Irish people are full members of society, and their faith deserves equal respect.
bank.ctx: This holds that Muslim Irish people are full members of society whose faith deserves equal respect.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are inherently more intelligent or capable than others. Mainstream science rejects it, and it is historically tied to ideologies like Nazism and systems like apartheid.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This is the principle of human equality: that no race is inherently smarter or more capable, and that the idea of a racial hierarchy is discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history.

bank.q: Ireland needs more Gardí on the streets and tougher sentences for violent crime.
bank.ctx: The Gardí are Ireland's police. This argues Ireland needs more of them on the streets and tougher sentences for violent crime.

bank.q: More police and longer sentences have never cut crime; prevention and services do.
bank.ctx: This argues more police and longer sentences have never cut crime, and that prevention and services do.

bank.q: Trans people should be able to change their legal gender by self-identification.
bank.ctx: This supports transgender rights: the view that people should be able to have the law recognise the gender they identify as, without needing medical approval.

bank.q: Biological sex is a reality the law should not let a declaration override.
bank.ctx: This is the gender-critical view: that biological sex is a fixed fact the law should not allow a personal declaration to override.

bank.q: Workers need stronger unions and rights, and a higher living wage.
bank.ctx: This supports stronger unions and worker rights, and a higher 'living wage'.

bank.q: Union power and higher mandated wages just cost jobs and hurt small businesses.
bank.ctx: This argues union power and higher mandated wages cost jobs and hurt small businesses.

bank.q: Ireland’s social welfare payments should be raised to protect people from poverty.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland's welfare payments should be raised to protect people from poverty.

bank.q: Raising welfare too far just weakens the incentive to work.
bank.ctx: This argues raising welfare too far weakens the incentive to work.

bank.q: Ireland over-regulates business; companies need less red tape and lower costs.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland over-regulates business and that companies need less red tape and lower costs.

bank.q: Cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment.
bank.ctx: This argues cutting regulation just lets companies off the hook on workers and the environment.

bank.q: Drug use should be decriminalised and treated as a health issue.
bank.ctx: This supports decriminalising drug use and treating it as a health issue.

bank.q: Going soft on drugs fuels addiction and disorder, and it should be resisted.
bank.ctx: This argues softening drug laws fuels addiction and disorder and should be resisted.

bank.q: Ireland should legalise assisted dying for the terminally ill.
bank.ctx: This supports legalising assisted dying (medical help to die) for the terminally ill.

bank.q: Assisted dying puts pressure on the vulnerable and crosses a line society should not cross.
bank.ctx: This argues assisted dying pressures the vulnerable and crosses a line society shouldn't cross.

bank.q: Ireland’s place is at the heart of a strong European Union.
bank.ctx: This sees Ireland's future at the heart of a strong European Union.

bank.q: Brussels has too much power over Ireland, and Irish sovereignty should come first.
bank.ctx: This argues Brussels (the EU) has too much power over Ireland and that Irish sovereignty should come first.

bank.q: Vulture funds and big investors should be blocked from buying up Irish homes.
bank.ctx: 'Vulture funds' are large investors that buy up property in bulk. This supports blocking them from buying Irish homes.

bank.q: Investment funds add much-needed housing supply, and blocking them would backfire.
bank.ctx: This argues investment funds add needed housing supply and that blocking them would backfire.

bank.q: Ireland’s system of many referendums on big questions is a strength worth keeping.
bank.ctx: Ireland changes its constitution by referendum and holds many. This argues that system is a strength worth keeping.

bank.q: Constant referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and cause needless division.
bank.ctx: This argues constant referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and cause needless division.

bank.q: Ireland should take a strong public stance for Palestinian rights, even at diplomatic cost.
bank.ctx: This supports Ireland taking a strong public stand for Palestinian rights, even at a diplomatic cost.

bank.q: Ireland should stay balanced on the Middle East rather than taking sides.
bank.ctx: This argues Ireland should stay balanced on the Middle East rather than taking sides.

bank.q: Protecting nature should take priority over new roads, data centres, and development.
bank.ctx: 'Data centres' are large computer facilities that use a lot of power. This puts protecting nature ahead of new roads, data centres, and development.

bank.q: Endless environmental objections are strangling the housing and infrastructure Ireland needs.
bank.ctx: This argues endless environmental objections block the housing and infrastructure Ireland needs.

bank.q: The government should intervene directly to cap energy and rent costs.
bank.ctx: This supports the government stepping in directly to cap energy and rent costs.

bank.q: Price caps cause shortages and drive suppliers out; they don’t fix the cost of living.
bank.ctx: This argues price caps cause shortages and drive suppliers out without fixing the real problem.

bank.q: Immigrants should adapt to Irish culture and values, not the other way around.
bank.ctx: This argues immigrants should adapt to Irish culture and values rather than the country adapting to them.

bank.q: A living culture is always a blend; demanding assimilation impoverishes Ireland.
bank.ctx: This argues a living culture is always a blend, so demanding assimilation impoverishes Ireland.

bank.q: Ireland should increase defence spending and take its own security more seriously.
bank.ctx: This supports higher defence spending and Ireland taking its own security more seriously.

bank.q: Money for the military is money that should go to housing and health instead.
bank.ctx: This argues money for the military would be better spent on housing and health.

bank.q: RTÉ and public broadcasting are worth funding and must stay independent.
bank.ctx: RTÉ is Ireland's public broadcaster. This argues it is worth funding and must stay independent.

bank.q: RTÉ is wasteful and out of touch, and its licence fee should be scrapped.
bank.ctx: This argues RTÉ is wasteful and out of touch and its licence fee should be scrapped.

bank.q: The unemployed are treated with too much suspicion; the safety net should be stronger.
bank.ctx: This argues the unemployed are treated with too much suspicion and the safety net should be stronger.

bank.q: Welfare too easily becomes a trap, and stricter conditions protect taxpayers who fund it.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare can trap people, and stricter conditions protect the taxpayers who fund it.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions carry the wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative view of tradition: that long-standing customs and institutions hold accumulated wisdom, so we should be cautious about sweeping them away for something new.

bank.q: Worshipping tradition just lets the dead govern the living and blocks necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply: that clinging to tradition for its own sake lets the past dictate to the present and blocks change that is needed.

bank.q: A good society depends more on personal responsibility than on government support.
bank.ctx: This reflects a right-leaning value: that a good society rests mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own lives, rather than leaning on government.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems the system creates is how the comfortable excuse others’ suffering.
bank.ctx: This reflects a left-leaning value: that many problems are caused by unfair systems, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable look past suffering they may benefit from.

heroTitle:

Irish politics?
heroSub: 70 statements on the issues defining Ireland right now: housing, immigration, a united Ireland, neutrality, and health. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, revealing both your party alignment and your framing bias.
